sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered why 2 + 3 * 4 equals 14 and not 20? Let's crack the code of how Java evaluates expressions!

• How Java decides the order of operations
• Why parentheses are your best friends
• How to avoid common calculation mistakes

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you're at a restaurant with a special order rule: drinks first, then appetizers, then main course. Java follows similar rules when evaluating expressions!

Java uses **operator precedence** - a set of rules that determines which operations happen first. Here's how it works:

• **Parentheses** always win - they're like putting something in a VIP section
• **Multiplication/Division** come next - they're the appetizers
• **Addition/Subtraction** come last - they're the main course

For example: `3 + 4 * 2` equals 11, not 14, because multiplication happens before addition.

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how Evaluating Expressions and Operator Precedence works:

steps.title: Parentheses First
steps.description: Java looks for parentheses and solves them first, starting from the innermost ones.

steps.title: Multiplication/Division
steps.description: Next, Java handles all multiplication and division from left to right.

steps.title: Addition/Subtraction
steps.description: Finally, Java does addition and subtraction from left to right.

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Parentheses always go first - use them to control order
✓ PEMDAS (Please Excuse My Dear Aunt Sally) helps remember the order
✓ When in doubt, add parentheses to make it clear

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use parentheses to make your intentions clear
Break complex expressions into smaller parts
Test your expressions with simple numbers first
donts: Don't rely on memory - use parentheses when unsure
Don't mix too many operations in one line
Don't forget that division comes before addition
sections.protip: When writing complex expressions, solve them on paper first to verify the order!

problem.description: Write a Java expression to calculate the average of three numbers (a, b, c) and then multiply it by a fourth number (d). What would be the result if a=5, b=10, c=15, and d=2?
hints: Parentheses can help group the average calculation
The average of three numbers is (a + b + c)/3
problem.explanation: First we calculate the average (5+10+15)/3 = 10, then multiply by 2 to get 20. Using 3.0 ensures we get a precise decimal result.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Operator precedence determines the order of operations in Java
📌 Practice breaking down complex expressions step by step
📌 You're now ready to tackle more complex calculations!
